blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Language models are now used to read central-bank text for economic forecasting, but most were trained on text written after the documents they read. A model reading a 2021 FOMC statement may already know that inflation rose in 2022, so part of its apparent skill can be memory of the outcome, a temporal form of test-set contamination. We measure this memory on FOMC statements and minutes from 2000 to 2026 by comparing modern open models with chronologically consistent models, which are trained only on text from before a fixed date. Asked about past GDP outcomes given only a date, models that cannot know the answer still reach an AUC of up to 0.64 from priors on dates and eras, so chance is the wrong baseline. Against these memory-free models on the same questions, most modern models recall which years had strong growth. Membership-inference scores sort documents by era and document type rather than by whether a model saw them, as exact counts in an open pretraining corpus show. In real-time nowcasts, every lookahead premium we estimate on US GDP is smaller than the forecast comparison can detect at macroeconomic sample sizes, and none on GDP or inflation survives correction for multiple testing. Lookahead audits should therefore measure memory directly against memory-free models on the same items.
blocks.zh: 语言模型现在被用来读取用于经济预测的中央银行文本,但大多数是在他们阅读的文件之后对文本进行培训的. 一个读出2021 FOMC声明的模型可能已经知道通货膨胀在2022年上升了,因此其明显的技能的一部分可以是对结果的记忆,一种测试定型污染的时间形式. 我们用FOMC的语句和从2000年到2026年的分钟来测量这个内存,将现代开放模型与时间顺序一致的模型进行比较,这些模型从固定日期之前开始只接受文字训练. 如果只问一个日期的过去GDP结果,无法知道答案的模型仍然从日期和时代的以往数据中得出最多为0.64的AUC,因此机会是错的基线。 对照这些在相同问题上的无记忆模型,大多数现代模型都记得那几年的强劲增长. 会员推论根据年代和文档类型对文件进行排序,而不是根据模型是否看到它们来评分,作为公开的预训节目中的准确计分. 在实时即时播报中,我们估计的美国GDP的每一次视差溢价都比预测的比较在宏观经济样本大小时所能发现的要小,而对于GDP或通货膨胀,都无法经受多重测试的纠正。 因此,Lookahead审计应直接对照相同物品上的无记忆模型衡量内存.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Language models are now used to read central-bank communication for forecasters, and
most of the models in use were trained on text written after the period they are asked
to read. A model that has seen the commentary of 2021 and 2022 does not need to infer
from a 2021 FOMC statement that inflation is about to rise; it can remember that it did.
In machine-learning terms this is temporal contamination, a form of test-set
contamination that runs through time: the outcomes a model is evaluated on appear in
text written after its inputs. Lookahead of
this kind has been documented in financial and economic prediction ( Sarkar and Vafa, 2024 ; Glasserman and Lin, 2024 ; Lopez-Lira et al., 2025 ; Gao et al., 2026 ; Eliseev and Seleznev, 2026 ) ,
and contamination by release date has been found in benchmark results ( Roberts et al., 2024 ) . Chronologically consistent models, trained only on text
available before a fixed date, now exist to remove it ( He et al., 2026 ; Yan et al., 2026 ) .

blocks.en:
We want to measure, for a forecasting task, how much of a model’s apparent skill is
memory, and whether that memory reaches the forecast when the forecast is made as it
would be in practice: in real time, on the data available that day, and scored against
the first published estimate. The usual checks are poorly suited to this. Scoring a
model against chance assumes that a model which has not seen the outcome guesses at
random. Membership-inference scores assume that the texts a model saw and the texts it
did not see differ only in that respect, an assumption that fails when the two come
from different periods ( Duan et al., 2024 ) . And a comparison of forecast accuracy with
and without the suspect model needs more data than a macroeconomic series provides.

blocks.en:
We build such a measurement for the FOMC’s statements and minutes from 2000 to 2026 and
for real-time nowcasts of US GDP and CPI growth from 2012 to 2024, and we score each
part of it against a reference other than chance. Date-only probes give a model a date
and ask about an outcome it could know only from later text. The reference is a set of
readers that cannot know the outcome, scored on the same items, and the inference allows
for outcomes that cluster in time and for priors on calendar words. A ladder of fixed
checkpoints from one chronologically consistent family asks whether a model does better
on outcomes its training could have contained than on outcomes it could not. Membership
scores ask whether a model saw a document; we check them against checkpoints with known
cutoffs and against exact counts in one model’s indexed training corpus. Finally, a
real-time nowcaster measures what the readings are worth, with a reader behind a
temporal gate as the control, two hard-data baselines, the professional nowcasts, and a
power analysis.

The first three of our six findings are positive results. The other three mark what
these data cannot resolve, and we report them with intervals and, for the forecast, the
smallest effect the test could detect. 1. Readers that cannot know the outcome do not score 0.5. On the GDP probe they reach
AUCs up to about 0.64 from priors on dates and eras, so every claim of memory
below compares a model with these readers on the same items. 2. The modern models remember outcomes that the memory-free readers cannot know.
Against the gated reader, six of the seven score higher after
adjusting for multiple comparisons. A date retrieves which years grew strongly. 3. Membership scores track era and document type rather than membership. Exact span
counts in OLMo-2’s indexed corpus date the end of its FOMC text to 2 November 2022, a year
before its model card’s cutoff, and within a year and a document type Min-K% does not
separate the documents found from those not found. 4. The probes cannot resolve finer distinctions. Within a year there are too few mixed
outcomes to tell whether a model remembers individual quarters. The modern models’
margins over ChronoGPT-2024, a small chronologically consistent model whose training also
runs past every outcome, do not survive adjustment for multiple comparisons, so whether
the larger models remember more than the small one stays open. The checkpoint ladder’s
intervals all include zero and are wider than that gap, which leaves open whether the
small models remember at all. 5. The forecast comparison lacks the power to detect a lookahead premium. The leaky
readers’ GDP premiums over the gated reader are a few percent of RMSE, below the
8.8 to 13.1 percent the test detects with 80% power, and their sign
depends on whether 2020 or 2021 is left out. They are also measured on a GDP nowcaster
that does not beat a running mean of past growth. 6. Text adds no skill that survives correction for multiple testing, either to the
real-time nowcaster or to the SPF, GDPNow and New York Fed nowcasts.

blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Memorisation grows log-linearly with model capacity, duplication and prompt length ( Carlini et al., 2023 ) . Detection methods ask whether a text was in the training
corpus: Min-K% Prob averages the log-probabilities of a text’s least likely tokens ( Shi et al., 2024 ) , Min-K%++ normalises them by the next-token distribution ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) , and guided prompts flag contamination when a completion matches a
reference instance ( Golchin and Surdeanu, 2024 ) . Contamination must be measured benchmark
by benchmark ( Sainz et al., 2023 ) , and answers to Stack Overflow questions are often
collages of memorised text whether or not the question predates training ( Caspari et al., 2025 ) ; Xu et al. (2024) and Ravaut et al. (2025) survey
the methods. Duan et al. (2024) find that membership inference barely beats chance on
Pile-trained models and trace reported successes to members and non-members drawn from
different periods. Our probes face the same confound, because answer priors track eras. We
ask whether a model knows an outcome that postdates a document, and score each leaky reader
against a gated reader and a persistence rule on the same items rather than against 0.5.

blocks.en:
Lookahead appears when models predict risk factors from earnings calls and election winners
from biographies ( Sarkar and Vafa, 2024 ) ; anonymising headlines improves GPT sentiment
trading in-sample, so distraction can outweigh lookahead ( Glasserman and Lin, 2024 ) ;
models recall economic series from before their cutoff even when told to respect a
historical boundary ( Lopez-Lira et al., 2025 ) ; and the probability of a non-unknown
answer given only a firm, ticker and date collapses after the cutoff ( Gao et al., 2026 ) . Telling a model to ignore what it knows leaves a 52% gap to true
ignorance ( Li et al., 2026 ) , no modern model passes the first fake-date test of Eliseev and Seleznev (2026) for macroeconomic forecasts, and the PaLM inflation forecasts of Faria-e Castro and Leibovici (2024) are in-sample for 2019–23. MACROCAST avoids leakage by
pretraining on synthetic series ( Carriero et al., 2026 ) , and Ludwig et al. (2026) state the general no-leakage condition. Most of this evidence concerns firm-level outcomes or
a model forecasting a series directly. We study a model reading central-bank text as one
input to a real-time nowcaster, price lookahead as a change in RMSE against first release,
and find that the memory a probe detects does not appear as resolvable forecast skill.

which is acceptable for estimation though it understates forecast uncertainty ( Lenza and Primiceri, 2022 ) . These text measures come from topic models, dictionaries or models

past the forecast period, so we make the reader’s training cutoff the variable under test.

blocks.en: 4 Measuring memory

blocks.en:
We measure memory three ways, each with its own null, before asking what memory
is worth in a forecast.
blocks.zh:

blocks.en:
A reader is given a date and nothing else, a two-answer form of the date-only recall
queries of Gao et al. (2026) . In the decision probe it is told that the
FOMC changed its target on that date and asked whether it raised or lowered it
(74 changes, 2000–2025). In the GDP probe it is asked whether
first-release real GDP growth in a given quarter was above or below 2 percent at an
annual rate (100 quarters, 2000–2024). A reader that has not seen the
outcome can only guess, but a guess need not score an AUC of 0.5: answer priors
can line up with eras in which one outcome was common, and a gated reader’s
checkpoint changes every January. The null is therefore set by two other readers scored
on the same items: the gated reader and a persistence rule that uses only what was
public before the item’s year began. Probe items cluster in time, so inference
respects the clustering: p p -values come from rotating the labels against the
scores in date order (a circular shift, which keeps the dependence in both
series), and intervals for AUC differences from resampling calendar years. We also
compare quarters with the same quarter number across years, tested by rotating the
years of the outcomes against the scores, and quarters within the same year, which
removes most between-era comparisons (a fourth quarter is dated by its release in the
following January, so it is read by the next gated checkpoint).

blocks.en: 5 Measuring what memory is worth
blocks.zh: 页:1 衡量记忆的价值

blocks.en:
We price memory by putting each reader’s signal into a real-time nowcaster, which
estimates growth in the current quarter before the official figure is published. At each origin the nowcaster takes one vintage of the eleven indicators.
Indicators are released with different delays, so the latest months are missing for
some series; this uneven end of the panel is the ragged edge. The nowcaster fills it
with forecasts from an autoregression of order two, AR(2), on each indicator’s own
monthly changes, averages to the quarter, and forms growth. It then reduces the
target’s own block of indicators (real activity for GDP, prices for CPI) to its first
three principal components, which we call block PCA, and regresses the target on these
three factors with a ridge penalty. This ridge regression is the bridge, the usual name
for a model that links monthly indicators to a quarterly target. It is estimated on the
quarters from 2000 Q1 whose first release is out by the origin. A text model adds the five dimensions of the
latest FOMC document published on or before the origin; training quarters take the
document available at the same position in their own quarter. Every regressor is
standardised by its training mean and standard deviation, so the penalty treats
every reader alike. The fill and the indicator blocks were chosen among six
specifications on a 2006–2011 hold-out; all six are reported on both windows
(Appendix A.5 ), and the order in which they were tried is stated there.

Text is only worth something if the hard-data model is competent, so we report two
further benchmarks. The first is a mixed-frequency dynamic factor model in the style of Bańbura and Modugno (2014) , fit by expectation maximisation on the same vintages
with the ragged edge left as missing data, which this estimator handles directly, and
with factor number and order chosen on the hold-out. The second is the set of professional nowcasts practitioners use: the Survey
of Professional Forecasters, GDPNow ( Higgins, 2014 ) and the New York Fed
Staff Nowcast ( Bok et al., 2018 ) , each used only where its value was public
on the date it carries: GDPNow from July 2014, when it went online, and the New
York Fed nowcast during its live publication, April 2016 to September 2021 and from
September 2023. We also ask directly whether a text signal corrects the
professional nowcasts, by regressing their first-release error on the signal out
of sample.

blocks.en:
The lookahead premium of a leaky reader is the percentage reduction in nowcast
RMSE of its text model against the gated reader’s text model, on the same
origins. Three origins share each target quarter. The primary test is the
Coroneo–Iacone test ( Coroneo and Iacone, 2020 ) , which compares the accuracy of two
forecasts and is built for small samples with autocorrelated errors. We run it two-sided, with
a weighted-periodogram estimate of the long-run variance, bandwidth m = ⌊ T 1 / 3 ⌋ m=\lfloor T^{1/3}\rfloor for T = 150 T=150{} origins and a Student- t t reference with 2 ​ m 2m degrees of freedom. As checks, we compute the Harvey–Leybourne–Newbold test ( Harvey et al., 1997 ) ,
a small-sample correction of the standard test of equal forecast accuracy, run with a
horizon of three origins, and a 95% interval from resampling quarters. The gain of a text model over the model without text is a nested
comparison, because the model without text is the text model with its text
coefficients set to zero. We test it with the one-sided Clark–West test ( Clark and West, 2007 ) , which adjusts the loss difference for the noise the
larger model adds by estimating coefficients that are zero under the null. Holm’s
method, a step-down version of the Bonferroni correction, adjusts each family of tests
for multiplicity: the
premium tests within each target, the 26 text-against-no-text tests across both
targets, and the 48 tests of text on top of the professional nowcasts. The minimum detectable effect is the premium the
primary test would detect with 80% power, from a quarter-block bootstrap standard
error of the mean loss difference and Student- t t quantiles with 2 ​ m 2m degrees of
freedom. We report the premium leaving out each year in turn, and a placebo for the
gated and ChronoGPT-2024 readers: the sequence of document signals is rotated against
the calendar, which keeps the signal’s distribution and persistence and breaks its
alignment with outcomes, legitimate information included.

The larger modern open models hold outcome memory that a date retrieves, beyond what
memory-free readers achieve on the same items. Whether the small chronologically
consistent models hold any is not resolvable with these probes. In a real-time nowcast,
neither the memory nor the text shows up as resolvable skill. A probe can show that a
model could use the future, but only a forecasting comparison can show that it does, and
at macroeconomic sample sizes that comparison has little power.
